clue.text: E.g. Hamlet's father's attempt to make rich cakes

parts.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, so he is an example of someone of that nationality
pa is an informal word for father, and the possessive 's adds a letter S
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Old King Hamlet tries his hand at baking something rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at the ghost in Shakespeare's play, but 'E.g. Hamlet's' just supplies the nationality and 'father's' is PA plus the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: These sweet flaky breakfast items are a kind of rich bakery cake.

parts.note: to dub is to call or name someone

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of yeti are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone doubts the rumour of a yeti sighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' looks like a summons to speak, but it means to name; 'out' signals the anagram of the creature's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubiety is doubt or uncertainty, a state of hesitant mistrust.

definitions.meaning: the ... is British slang for jail, so to be in the ... is to be locked up

explanation.walkthrough: 'in prison' defines the word as in the British phrase 'in the nick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch cut in wood is a small scratch; British slang also calls a police station or jail by this name.

clue.text: Dark except when second comes first

indicators.note: comes first tells us the letter for second is placed at the front of the charade

parts.note: unless means except when, or except if

explanation.surface: A rule about when it gets dark, with an exception tied to timing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes first' puts S ahead of UNLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A place with no sunshine is gloomy and without light.

clue.text: He picks recipe to make us quite hungry?

indicators.note: a recipe is a mixture of ingredients, so it tells us to mix up the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A man choosing a recipe to whet the appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' is the signal to rearrange HEPICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly in need of a snack is being mildly hungry.

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the word for sleep is set to follow the abbreviation for Sunday

parts.note: kip is British slang for a sleep or nap

explanation.surface: A man called Bob enjoying a Sunday lie-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name but is a verb: to bob along is to move lightly, as when one skips.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob and to hop lightly along are both bouncing movements.

indicators.note: something that goes wrong breaks down, so the letters of car-dial are scrambled

explanation.surface: The dial on a car's dashboard fails, which ought to be a simple fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges the letters of CARDIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something root-level or fundamental is elemental in nature.

clue.text: Nation's exhibition? Still remains to be seen!

definitions.text: Nation's exhibition? Still remains to be seen!

parts.words: Nation's exhibition? Still remains to be seen!
parts.note: a national collection in London where ancient relics, the 'remains', are put on show for visitors to see

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still remains to be seen' reads as 'not yet decided', but it means ancient remains can still be viewed there.
explanation.definitionFit: A great London institution displaying the country's collection of antiquities.

clue.text: Man in charge of changing to steam trains?

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of to steam trains are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A railway official overseeing the switch from older engines to steam power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges TOSTEAMTRAINS; the official is in charge of the stop where trains call.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who runs a railway stop is its manager or supervisor.

parts.note: to rub something is to polish it
an icon is an image or likeness

explanation.surface: Someone cleaning a picture of an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality, but it is the verb meaning to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: The small river in northern Italy that Caesar crossed is a watercourse there.

clue.text: World War II fighter crashed in ditch

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters of in ditch are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A wartime fighter plane comes down in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighter' suggests an aircraft, but the soldiers of a British special force in Burma were so called.
explanation.definitionFit: These were members of a long-range jungle force fighting in Burma in 1943-45.

clue.text: They're found nailed below the arch

definitions.text: They're found nailed below the arch

parts.words: They're found nailed below the arch
parts.note: the 'arch' is the arch of the foot, and the digits beyond it each carry a nail

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something hammered under an archway; the arch is part of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The digits of the foot sit forward of its arch and have nails.

clue.text: This girl became sick on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back tells us the word for became sick is read from right to left

parts.note: to fall ill is to have ailed

explanation.surface: A girl fell ill on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns AILED round.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, as in the cookery writer Ms Smith.

indicators.note: the letters are collected from inside the word that follows, a run lying within it

explanation.surface: Revenue officers taking tax from nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected from' points to the run inside DISCOTHEQUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot is an old word for a payment or levy, as in 'scot-free'.

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A huge bird that has been named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these were a race of colossal deities; the word now means any huge person or thing.

clue.text: Nurse Cavell worked out this hospital diet

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters of diet are reorganised

explanation.surface: A famous nurse devises a diet for her hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' signals the anagram. Edith Cavell was a British nurse executed in 1915 for helping Allied soldiers escape occupied Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the British First World War nurse Cavell.

parts.note: obstacles found on a golf course, where an opponent's ball once blocked one's putting line

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally', but means 'on the golf course'.
explanation.definitionFit: In old golf rules, a ball blocking another's line to the hole was the name for that obstruction; the word now means any hindrance.

parts.note: to have hid something is to have obscured it

indicators.note: possibly signals that goal may be rearranged into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A Spanish player's view of the goal was blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram; 'obscured' supplies a past tense, not an adjective describing the goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a Spanish nobleman of the lower gentry.

annotationWithheld.why: One settling for motorway subsidy: M (motorway) + GRANT (subsidy) needs I, which only 'One' can give, but 'One' is also needed in the definition 'One settling'; one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Moses' old lady with the brush

definitions.text: Moses' old lady with the brush

parts.words: Moses' old lady with the brush
parts.note: an American folk painter, Anna Mary Robertson, took up painting in old age and was known by a family title before the surname Moses

explanation.walkthrough: The Biblical Moses is a false lead: this is the elderly American painter known as Grandma Moses.
explanation.definitionFit: The family title given to a grandmother, and the nickname of the painter.

definitions.meaning: an overcoat worn over other clothes
the last layer of paint a decorator applies

explanation.definitionFit: Both an overcoat worn outermost and the final layer of paint, each being the outermost covering.

clue.text: Conference centre where insane stay in retirement?

indicators.note: retirement is a withdrawal or going back, so the words for insane and stay are read backwards

parts.note: mad means insane
to stop somewhere is to stay there

explanation.surface: A rest home where the mentally ill may stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns MADSTOP round. Potsdam, near Berlin, hosted the Allied conference of 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city hosted the 1945 Allied summit, so it was a meeting venue.

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A march in support of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a full international match in cricket, the bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: A public march or rally is a protest.

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and a name for the underworld itself
a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A girl from the criminal underworld loses her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' suggests gangsters, but here it is Dis, the Roman realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire an employee is to let them go from their job.

definitions.meaning: an official stamp or mark pressed into wax
a marine mammal that balances balls on its nose in a circus act

explanation.definitionFit: An impressed emblem on a document; also a whiskered sea mammal trained to do tricks.

definitions.meaning: the racecourse in Surrey where the Derby is run, on chalk hills called downs
a laxative made of magnesium sulphate, named after a Surrey spring

explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south of London; its downs are rolling chalk hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A Surrey town giving its name both to a racecourse on its chalk hills and to a bath and laxative mineral.

parts.note: Oxford's colour is dark blue, and a flower here is something that flows, a river

explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' suggests a bloom but means a river; Oxford University's sporting colour is dark blue, and the Thames there has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the Thames as it passes through Oxford.

indicators.note: to release means to let go, so the word for boy is let out of surgeon

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A medical request to discharge a young patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to release' removes S, O and N from SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone to act is to spur them on.

parts.note: May is a month of spring
love means zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A region known for romance in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish county in Connacht.

clue.text: Orient's capital ploughed into ground and stand

indicators.note: ploughing churns up soil, so the letters of ground are churned together with the letter

parts.note: the Orient is the East, whose capital letter is E

explanation.surface: A farmer turning soil into land in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ploughed into' mixes E with GROUND. 'capital' suggests a city, but it is a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear or endure something is to put up with it.

clue.text: How cunning-counterfeit visa brought in the night before!

indicators.note: brought in tells us one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: eve is the evening before a festival

indicators.note: a counterfeit is a fake, so the letters of visa are falsified into a new order

explanation.surface: A forged visa is smuggled in on the night before travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counterfeit' signals the anagram and 'brought in' the insertion; 'How' is a link at the head of an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shifty and avoiding straight answers is a crafty, slippery quality.

clue.text: Complaints coming between Jeremiah and Ezekiel

definitions.meaning: an Old Testament book placed in the Bible between the books of those two prophets

explanation.definitionFit: Laments are cries of sorrow; the Bible book of that name follows Jeremiah and precedes Ezekiel.
